This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
Tiny Breakout: 0.05 ns after placement, not the template's 0.1. Most of the delay cells
hold repair added were only to reach the extra margin: 135 of them at 0.1 ns, 46 at 0.05.
With 0.1 the design with the sound got stuck in detailed routing (~4,300 violations);
with 0.05 it routed clean, hold slack +0.028 ns at the worst corner. That slack is on top
of sign-off's own 0.25 ns clock uncertainty and 5% derate. Don't go below 0.05.
Tiny Breakout: routing at ~81% utilisation, with the sound. With the defaults, detailed
routing got stuck at ~4,600 violations. The global router reserves 10% of each layer's
tracks instead of 30%, and synthesis uses ABC's AREA 1 script instead of AREA 0: with both
it routed with 0 DRC, LVS and antenna errors at 80.4% (AREA 0 also routed, at 81.2%).
Tiny Breakout: let synthesis use sky130's drive-strength-1 cells (nand2_1, dfxtp_1, ...).
The PDK's default list excludes them for routability, so every gate was a _2 cell. This
list, without them, gave 22% less cell area, better timing and a clean route (measured
before the sound was added: 80.5% -> 61% utilisation); synthesis still honours the PDK's
list of cells with layout problems.
Tiny Breakout: keep the resizer from using sky130's clock delay cells as ordinary buffers.
Only two of them are excluded by default. Measured before the sound was added, it picked
clkdlybuf4s25_1 (10 um2, slow by design) for 51 fanout and input buffers; with these
excluded it used buf_1 (3.75 um2), saving ~290 um2. Hold repair uses dlygate4sd3_1, which
stays available.
Tiny Breakout: small clock buffers. The leaf buffers take the root buffer's type. Measured
before the sound was added, the default clkbuf_16 root gave 32 clkbuf_16 leaves driving
5-6 flip-flops each (1,076 um2 of clock tree); clkbuf_4/2 gave ~400 um2, no clock-pin slew
violations and +0.01-0.02 ns skew. clkbuf_2 throughout was smaller still but left clock
pins over their slew limit.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
